NEW DEFECT DISCOVERED DURING THIS TODO'S VERIFICATION (out of this
TODO's scope_limit to fix -- benchbox/core/ is not in
scope_limit.only_modify): TPC-H throughput mode fails row-count
validation for queries 11, 16, 18, and 20 on EVERY stream, at SF=1 on
DuckDB, regardless of --seed choice (reproduced with seed=42, seed=7,
and no seed at all). Confirmed independent of concurrency: the
identical 4 queries fail identically in single-stream POWER mode with
a non-reference seed; POWER mode with no seed (qgen-defaults, exact
validation against the official answer files) passes cleanly. Root
cause hypothesis: benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py derives each
stream's per-query seed as `seed + stream_id * 1000 + position`, so no
throughput stream (beyond possibly the first query of stream 0) can
ever land on the reference-seed exact-match path; every throughput
query therefore falls back to LOOSE (+-50%) tolerance
(benchbox/core/expected_results/tpch_results.py), which is not wide
enough for these 4 TPC-H-spec-sanctioned non-deterministic queries.
tpch_results.py's own docstring flags RANGE mode as "reserved for
future use" and not yet wired up for TPC-H -- likely the intended fix.
Previously invisible because the throughput driver was only ever
tested against Mock connections before throughput-real-db-integration-tests,
and that TODO's new SF=0.01 tests don't hit this SF=1-scale manifestation.
Flagged as a background task (task_c4fffdd0) for a follow-up session
with full repro details and a docstring typo also noticed in passing
(tpch_results.py misstates the reference seed's decimal value).

Decision: use key-aware, parenthesis-aware post-processing of the existing DuckDB DDL, not full structured regeneration and not the stranded greedy regex. Evidence across TPC-DS dict/list schemas, DataVault object schemas, vector_search list schemas, and NYC/TSBS dict-of-columns schemas shows no uniform ColumnDefinition input seam. create_schema intentionally requests DuckDB DDL to retain PKs, while replacing it with ClickHouseDDLGenerator would re-render every column and violate byte-identical non-nullable DDL. A local top-level column scanner can wrap only source-nullable, non-key type spans, preserve all other bytes, and correctly keep mid-list DECIMAL(10,2) boundaries.

Nullable wrapping excludes source PK metadata plus resolved PRIMARY KEY/PARTITION BY/ORDER BY references. Tuning identifiers are normalized to actual DDL case. Real chDB created all 24 TPC-DS business tables plus dbgen_version; focused suite 99/99 and tuned gate 1/1 pass.

Parenthesis-aware top-level column scanning preserves compact mid-list DECIMAL(10,2) boundaries; selected type-span edits leave other bytes untouched. Contradictory source-nullable plus NOT NULL raises ValueError, and pre-existing Nullable types are not double-wrapped.

detail.evidence: Confirmed .github/workflows/pr.yml:564 timeout-minutes: 30 for medium-test. Sampled the last 20 pr.yml runs via the Actions API: 19 succeeded, 1 cancelled at 30.3min (PR #1306, twice). Successful wall times (min): 20.2 21.4 21.5 21.8 26.5 26.8 26.8 26.9 26.9 27.4 27.6 29.2 29.5 29.6 29.6 29.8 29.8 29.9 29.9 -- min=20.2, median=27.4, max=29.9, p95=29.9. Eight of nineteen runs land at >=29.2min, i.e. within 48s of the cap; the max successful run finished 6s under it. IMPORTANT caveat: this distribution is CENSORED -- any run that would have exceeded 30min was cancelled and is excluded from the successful set, so the true upper tail is unknown and >=30. p95*1.3 = 38.9min, so 40 is the smallest round value meeting the >=30% headroom rule without the 'huge value' anti-pattern.

Raised .github/workflows/pr.yml medium-test timeout-minutes 30 -> 40, sized to observed p95 29.9min * 1.3 = 38.9 rounded up. Six-line inline comment records the sizing RULE, the 2026-07-25 measurement, the metrics warning hook and a pointer to docs/operations/fast-lane-budget.md for the censoring caveat and resize history. Explicitly not a 'never think about it again' value per the anti-pattern -- 40 keeps the timeout meaningful as a hang backstop. detail.evidence: Repointed the patch from the string target 'benchbox.cli.main.get_config_manager' to patch.object(_main_module, 'get_config_manager'), resolving the module once via sys.modules - the same indirection the file already uses for _run_module and that test_quiet_mode.py:19 uses for _main_mod. Root cause is not a missing attribute: benchbox/cli/__init__.py caches the main() FUNCTION into globals under the submodule's name, so on Python 3.10 (unittest.mock._importer walks with getattr) the target resolves to <function main> which has no get_config_manager. Python >= 3.11 masks it via pkgutil.resolve_name. Replayed 3.10's resolver against the real package: package-only import then attribute access yields <function main>, has get_config_manager=False (pre-fix) vs module/True (post-fix); a minimal same-shape package on a real 3.10.17 interpreter reproduces the nightly's exact message. Replaced the private byte probe with the shared benchbox.utils.file_format.has_trailing_delimiter (already used by every other reader; reads text-mode so CRLF is normalized, and compares field counts rather than matching a byte tail). Proven across 4 framings (LF/CRLF x trailing/clean) - private probe was wrong only on CRLF+trailing; shared helper correct in all 4. Rung 1: 29 passed -n 0.

No regex change was needed - the unit's premise (cross-platform error-message drift) was a misdiagnosis. Proven: _read_tbl_files() runs before _sort_table(), so on CRLF input pyarrow raised ArrowInvalid ('CSV parse error: Expected 2 columns, got 3') before the ValueError could be raised. pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) therefore failed on exception TYPE, not on message text; the messages are identical on all platforms. Both asserts pass once w1 fixes the framing probe. Added test_crlf_source_still_reports_unknown_sort_column to pin the validation-outranks-framing ordering, plus test_reads_trailing_delimiter_tbl_with_crlf_line_endings; both write explicit CRLF bytes so the Windows-only framing is now exercised on every platform. The recipe prints whatever its own shell considers the path to be; on Windows that shell is Git Bash/MSYS, which renders C:\\Users\\... as /c/Users/.... The assertion compared that against Path.resolve()'s native spelling, so it failed on spelling alone. Replaced the substring check with an exact comparison on a canonical form: normalize_path() lowercases and translates a leading /X/ drive segment, but ONLY when os.name == 'nt' - on POSIX a leading single-letter segment like /a/b is an ordinary directory and must not be rewritten. emitted_worktree_path() additionally asserts exactly one WORKTREE_PATH= line, so this is strictly stronger than the substring test it replaces. Verified both branches by exercising normalize_path directly against the literal strings from the nightly log: emitted '/c/Users/runneradmin/AppData/.../BenchBox.pool-01' and native 'C:\\Users\\runneradmin\\AppData\\...\\BenchBox.pool-01' now compare equal under os.name='nt', while under posix '/a/b/c' is untouched and case is preserved. Platform-gated rather than 'fixed', because the test is POSIX-only by construction and the behaviour it exercises does not exist on Windows. It shims git with an extensionless '#!/bin/sh' script placed first on PATH, but Windows resolves git.exe/git.cmd and never executes an extensionless file, so the shim is bypassed entirely; it then drives the recipe's INT trap with 'kill -INT $PPID', which has no Windows equivalent. The nightly evidence matches exactly: returncode 0 with stderr "Switched to a new branch 'feature/signal-test'" - the real git ran, the claim succeeded, and there was no interrupt to trap, so 'assert result.returncode != 0' failed as 'assert 0 != 0'. Added pytest.mark.skipif(os.name == 'nt') to the module pytestmark with that reasoning as the skip reason. POSIX behaviour is untouched: the test still runs and passes on macOS/Linux (4 passed locally), and no script under _project/scripts was modified.

detail.evidence: Added TestHasTrailingDelimiterFraming to tests/unit/utils/test_file_format.py - has_trailing_delimiter had NO direct unit test before this; the only coverage was indirect, via three platform test files. Pins all four framing/terminator cells (CRLF+trailing True, CRLF+clean False, LF+trailing True, LF+clean False) against BOTH checkers: the column_names field-count path that all ten platform callers use, and the column_names=None ends-with fallback, which is reachable but taken by no current caller. Plus a realistic multi-row CRLF file and a file with leading blank CRLF lines. Fixtures are explicit bytes so CRLF is exercised on every platform, not only the Windows nightly leg. 10 tests, all passing.

Gave _write_tbl_crlf a trailing_delimiter flag (default True, so the two existing callers are unchanged) and added test_reads_clean_tbl_with_crlf_line_endings - the fourth cell of the writer's matrix. It asserts the output schema is exactly ['id','l_shipdate'], i.e. no synthetic trailing column survives on input that has none. Honest note on what this case does and does not catch: under a simulated binary-read regression it PASSES, because a failed probe returns False and clean input needs no synthetic column. It guards the opposite direction - a probe that wrongly reports a trailing delimiter would add a column to an N-field file and fail here. The trailing-delimiter cases catch false negatives; this catches false positives. Together they pin both.

Stated the requirement where it lives, in _check_first_nonempty_line's docstring: TEXT MODE IS REQUIRED, NOT INCIDENTAL, with the causal chain spelled out - both reads open 'rt', universal newlines translate CRLF to LF before the checker, and every checker strips only backslash-n, so a binary read leaves a stray CR that adds a phantom field, breaks the ends-with match, and on bytes makes rstrip raise, which the blanket except turns into a confident 'no trailing delimiter'. Points at the test that enforces it. The enforcement is behavioural, not a source grep: simulating the regression by switching the uncompressed read to 'rb' fails 6 of the 10 framing tests and 2 of the 3 writer CRLF tests. Verified and reverted; file restored byte-for-byte.

Two independent CRLF bugs in benchbox/core/tpch/generator.py; benchbox/utils/file_format.py was NOT needed despite being in scope. (1) _has_trailing_delimiter read the last two bytes and matched b'|\\n', which a CRLF file never matches - its tail is b'|\\r\\n' - so a Windows file was classified already-clean and never rewritten. Now reads three bytes and rstrips the terminator before looking for the delimiter, the same shape as the sorting.py fix in PR #1332. (2) The streaming rewrite replaced only b'|\\n', so even a detected CRLF file would have kept every delimiter; it now replaces b'|\\r\\n' and b'|\\n', preserving the terminator as found. The carry also had to grow from one byte to two, because a chunk boundary can fall inside '|\\r\\n' and a one-byte carry splits '|' from '\\r\\n'. Added six byte-explicit CRLF tests so both framings run on every platform, not just the Windows leg: detect+strip, interior empty fields, already-clean CRLF byte-stable (the must-preserve, including that terminators are not rewritten to LF), idempotence, an unterminated '|\\r' final row, and a chunk-boundary test that sweeps EVERY chunk size from 1 to len(payload). Proven to fail: reverting both fixes fails 5 of the 6; reverting ONLY the two-byte carry fails exactly the chunk-boundary test. tests/unit/core/tpch/ 295 passed. Fast lane 26085/26550.

detail.evidence: DECISION: maintenance mode (leased write freeze), with verified quiescence demoted to a corroborating probe. Rationale: quiescence alone is unsound - it samples the past and cannot bind the future, and the cutover window is minutes. Evidence this session: three reads 5min apart were identical (events count=4440 last_seq=4440 latest=2026-07-31T16:38:10Z), yet the DB had still moved 1720->1726 items and 4424->4440 events earlier the same day, and joe@joe-mac-mini.local holds a live claim. 'Quiet now' is not 'quiet during the restore'. Reconcile-after was rejected: restore-legacy --replace destroys interleaved writes silently and the rebuilt chain re-hashes clean from the snapshot, so there is no post-hoc signal to reconcile against. Implemented as a leased freeze (todo freeze / --status / --release) gating every mutating command in main(); TTL-expiry satisfies the no-stuck-lock must-preserve, and a no-freeze DB is unaffected. Also added stats['events'] write-activity fingerprint - the quiescence probe was previously unimplementable (see w2 note). 32 new tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_todo_db_freeze.py; full suite 1233 passed.

(2) Findings loss: Joe chose option A, carry them. SOLVED - todo-db #1 (restore_legacy carries findings, rejects unknown tables, migration 005) and BenchBox #1361 (snapshot widened 12->17 tables). (3) Concurrency PRECONDITION SUPERSEDED 2026-07-31: this item's must-preserve says 'never restore --replace while another actor holds a live claim'. That test is WRONG and is falsified with evidence - claims cover only claim/start/done/complete on existing items, while create/defer/promote/block/config writes take NO claim, and two items were created mid-window by an unclaimed actor. must-preserve is create-time-only and this item has 5 dependents, so it is superseded here rather than re-created. THE OPERATIVE PRECONDITION IS NOW: hold a leased maintenance freeze ('todo freeze --reason ... --ttl H', added in the tracker-cutover-needs-a-write-freeze-not-a-claim-check branch) for the whole snapshot->restore window, corroborated by a stable stats['events'] fingerprint across two reads. A claim check alone MUST NOT be used to gate the destructive step. (4) Moving target: destination schema changed v3->v4 mid-flight. detail.evidence: Race reproduced against live state: detect_orphaned_commits.py flags 5 orphans across 3 branches, including my own b5c56ea9 from PR #1503. GUARD POINT DECIDED: detection, not prevention. auto-merge-on-open.yml already re-evaluates on synchronize and revokes for soundness paths, but it cannot prevent this race - there is no later push to react to until after the merge has already happened. A detector for exactly this class already exists (orphaned-commit-detector.yml, whose header records three earlier occurrences); the gap is cadence, not absence. It ran weekly, so up to seven days of develop silently missing a change. Withholding auto-merge was rejected: the item's must-preserve requires an ordinary fully-pushed PR to keep merging hands-free.

Removed the paths filter from the detector's develop push trigger so it runs on EVERY develop push - the moment a squash merge can strand a commit - keeping the weekly schedule as a backstop for branches pushed long after their PR closed. Allowlisted b5c56ea9 (my own #1503 orphan, content re-landed verbatim via #1504).

PR #1538, commit ec03398741. DECIDED: retain published-results history, do not rewrite. Recorded as docs/development/adr/adr-published-results-history-retention.md with the measured exposure (183/207 bundles leaking, 206/207 raw machine_id, public repo), the rationale, and the alternatives rejected. Reasoning: a force-push cannot retract already-public content - clones, forks and cached commit views survive it - so it converts a known exposure into an exposure plus a false belief it was undone, while breaking every clone and fork of a branch whose purpose is external consumption. Exposure class is machine-local absolute paths and usernames, not secrets; credentials and connection strings are redacted on a separate path that was working correctly. The ADR states explicitly that the decision does NOT extend to a higher severity class - a credential, token or customer data is a rotate-then-decide situation where rewriting may be justified because the secret can actually be invalidated - and points at salt rotation as the cheaper way to change published pseudonym identity without touching history.

detail.evidence: Trigger gap confirmed by enumerating every workflow with a pull_request trigger: auto-merge-on-open, extension-smoke, gitignore-lint, pr.yml -> [develop]; docs, results-explorer-browser -> [release, develop]; lint, perf-smoke, test, validate-release-pr -> [release]; validate-submission -> [published-results]. A feature-branch base matches none, so the PR triggers nothing and shows an empty check list. DECIDED: detect, not prevent. A make pr-open refusal only covers PRs opened through that path - the web UI, gh pr create and other tooling bypass it - whereas a workflow with no branch filter is authoritative for every PR however created. Prevention in pr-open remains a possible addition, not a substitute.

Six have NO consumer in any of the three: machine_id, working_dir, driver_runtime_python_executable, database_path, data_path, engine_host. They account for roughly 1320 of the 1615 pseudonym occurrences. Three do: submission_path (contract only), database_name (Explorer app), endpoint (pipeline, app, and contract). The read model has no machine or host column at all, so the grouping these pseudonyms were introduced to protect - the stated motivation for #1512 - is not implemented anywhere. Confirms the reframe: for the six, not publishing dominates salting, because a pseudonym with no reader is pure liability and the transform is a public confirmation oracle.

Recorded as docs/development/adr/adr-published-identifier-field-set.md, Accepted. Decision: do not publish the six identifier fields with no consumer (machine_id, working_dir, driver_runtime_python_executable, database_path, data_path, engine_host); remove them at the publication boundary rather than pseudonymising them. Keep publishing pseudonyms for the three with readers (endpoint, database_name, submission_path) and leave the salt question open for those. Alternatives recorded with reasons: minting a default salt (rejected as primary - does not close the oracle for already-published bytes and keeps paying a privacy cost for data nothing reads; still right for the three with readers), and accepting the oracle (rejected - the exposure scales with contributors, and choosing to publish confirmable identifiers on their behalf is not ours to make silently). The ADR states the id-rotation consequence explicitly and that this supersedes #1537's field set so ids rotate once, not twice.

detail.title: Corpus bundles carry no EOL attribute, so a CRLF checkout breaks byte identity
PRs into published-results receive zero CI, including the base guard added to catch exactly this

detail.evidence:
Verified end-to-end on 2026-08-05 against live state, not a declared baseline.

LIVE RULESET: 'gh api repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/rulesets/15611785' reports required_status_checks contexts ['ci-required-result', 'Results Explorer browser gate']. The flip is applied.

LIVE DRIFT CHECK: Release Canary run 30997653699 on develop, job 'ruleset drift', conclusion success, completed 2026-08-05T10:30:50Z - after the flip. That job runs scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py against the real GitHub API and fails the workflow on drift, so it is the rung that actually observes live state.

CORRECTION to this item's earlier blocked note: it credited tests/unit/test_ruleset_drift.py with going green on apply. That test compares synthetic ruleset payloads against the contexts declared in docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md and never calls the API, so it exercises the comparison logic and would have passed whether or not the flip happened. It remains meaningful - it pins that the runbook declares both contexts and that a missing context IS reported as drift - but it is not the live check. It passes: 6 tests.

THE CONTEXT ACTUALLY REPORTS: merged PR #1567's rollup shows 'Results Explorer browser gate: SUCCESS'. This was the real hazard of the flip - a required context that never reports blocks every PR forever - and it is disproved on a real PR that merged after the flip.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: PRs based on published-results still receive zero checks, so the gate does not cover them. Logged separately as published-results-prs-receive-zero-ci-20260805 rather than left implicit in this item.

Reproduced, and it downgrades this item's own premise.

ARITHMETIC MATCH: 207 primary bundles under results-data/bundles (excluding companion suffixes and the migration manifest), and all 207 are multi-line. Windows nightly reported exactly 207 failures. Every scanned bundle fails there, so the cause is systematic, not per-bundle content.

DIVERGENCE REPRODUCED: for a bundle whose stored LF bytes re-derive byte-identically, converting the bytes to CRLF (what core.autocrlf=true produces on checkout) makes canonical_json_bytes(anonymize(json.loads(...))) differ from the on-disk bytes: 7522 re-derived vs 7777 stored, a 255-byte gap equal to the file's 255 lines. json.loads parses both forms to the SAME dict, so this is purely an encoding-level divergence with identical logical content.

CORRECTION - the result_id hazard I asserted when filing this item is WRONG. I claimed publishing from a Windows checkout would derive different result IDs for identical content. It would not. pipeline.py:655 sets public_raw = canonical_json_bytes(public_bundle) and passes that to result_id_from_bundle as raw, so the sha8 in the result_id is computed over the canonical re-encoding, which emits LF regardless of how the source file was checked out. Line 722 then writes those same canonical bytes. Publication output and result IDs are therefore EOL-stable, and I did not check that before asserting it.

WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, at correspondingly lower severity: results-data/** has no text/eol attribute, so working-tree bytes are platform-dependent. That (a) makes the byte-identity test pass on Linux and macOS and fail on Windows, which is why it landed green and went red in the next nightly, and (b) lets a contributor on a translating checkout commit CRLF bundles that then permanently disagree with what publication emits - breaking the in-tree invariant and producing spurious whole-file diffs. It is a repo-hygiene and test-portability defect, not a content-addressing one.

SCOPE CHECK for the fix: results-data holds 400 .json, 4 .md, 1 .py, plus .gitkeep/.gitignore - all text, no binary - so pinning the whole tree to LF is safe.

Fixed in 1302c1accc.

CHANGE: .gitattributes gains '/results-data/** text eol=lf'. Chose the attribute over a newline-insensitive comparison in the test, because the weaker test goes green while still allowing a contributor on a translating checkout to commit CRLF bundles that permanently disagree with what publication emits.

NO CORPUS PERTURBATION: 'git add --renormalize results-data' stages 0 files, so every tracked corpus blob is already LF in the index. The attribute is purely forward-looking - no bundle bytes change, so no digest and no result_id moves. This was the main risk of the fix and it is disproved rather than assumed.

TEST: tests/unit/scripts/test_corpus_privacy_invariant.py::test_corpus_checks_out_with_lf_on_every_platform asserts every git-tracked path under results-data resolves eol=lf, via 'git ls-files -z' piped into 'git check-attr -z --stdin eol'. It sits next to the byte-identity gate it protects.

FALSIFIED: with .gitattributes reverted to develop's version and the test unchanged, the test FAILS - 'git check-attr eol' reports 'unspecified' and the assertion lists all tracked corpus files. Restoring the attribute makes it pass. So the test observes the fix, not merely the presence of new code.

SUITES: tests/unit/scripts/test_corpus_privacy_invariant.py 9 passed; tests/unit/scripts 1493 passed. check-scope: OK, 2 changed files, both inside only_modify.

RESIDUAL: this pins the attribute, which is the mechanism git actually uses. It does not prove the outcome on a real Windows checkout - I have no Windows host - so the nightly matrix remains the confirming observation. Expect tomorrow's Nightly Validation to drop test_rederived_corpus_publishes_byte_identically_to_what_is_stored from its windows-latest failures while the 7 pre-existing MCP durable-jobs failures persist.

DECISION (Joe, 2026-08-05): a privacy rejection ABORTS the build.

Chosen over two alternatives that were put to him explicitly:
- Publish the clean bundles and exit non-zero with a distinct summary. Rejected: it means a red build can still deploy a snapshot, and it is more machinery for the same safety property.
- Keep the skip but escalate logging and record rejections in the manifest. Rejected: the corpus still silently loses results, which is the defect itself.

Aborting matches the precedent already in this file. DuplicateResultIdError (pipeline.py:52) was made deliberately NOT a ValueError for exactly this reason, and its docstring states the rule: something a human must resolve in the corpus is not a bundle to drop. A privacy rejection is the same class - the detector fired, so a human needs to look.

SITES FOUND - three, all in pipeline.py, and the third behaves differently from the other two:
- 217, in _public_applied_receipt: leaking applied receipt.
- 230, in _public_bundle_data: leaking bundle.
- 738, in the plans companion block: leaking plans sidecar. This one is caught by its OWN inner handler at 746, not the loop handler at 766, so today it drops the plans companion and publishes the bundle anyway. Same silent-detector-fired condition, different blast radius.

All three currently raise ValueError, which the loop catches at 766 alongside JSONDecodeError, KeyError and TypeError, and downgrades to 'skipped_bundles += 1' plus a logger.warning.

CONFIRMED NO BROADER SWALLOW: pipeline.py and build_results_explorer_snapshot.py contain no 'except Exception' or 'except BaseException', so a non-ValueError propagates out of the build rather than being caught further up.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: pipeline.py:216 raises ValueError when the applied receipt cannot be sanitized at all. That is a malformed-input condition rather than a privacy rejection, so it keeps the skip. Worth its own look - an unsanitizable receipt is arguably the same state a leaky one is in - but changing it is a different decision and is not covered by this item's premise.

detail.evidence:
Implemented in f96d546262, PR #1569.

CHANGE: PrivacyRejectionError(Exception) - deliberately not a ValueError - raised at all three find_public_path_leaks sites (pipeline.py 217/230/738). It escapes both the plans block's own handler at 746 and the per-bundle handler at 766, so the build stops.

SCOPE HELD: pipeline.py:232 still raises ValueError when an applied receipt cannot be sanitized at all. That is malformed input rather than a privacy rejection, and promoting it would turn every corrupt sidecar into a build outage. A must-preserve test pins that a malformed companion is still only a warning.

Enumerated all ~24 ci-lint guards (26 physical commands; some share a failure tag). Exactly TWO are environment-inapplicable on a GitHub-hosted runner:

- agent-identity (agent-identity-check): resolves 'git config user.*'. An ephemeral runner has none. Post-#1558 an absent identity returns [] and passes; the recipe also injected a synthetic 'BenchBox CI' identity. Either input makes the check incapable of failing, so it verifies nothing there. pr.yml's code-lint job already omits it for the same reason.
- skill-sync-check: shells out to $(SKILL_SYNC), which Makefile:747 defines as '/Users/joe/Developer/skill-sync/dist/cli/index.js' - a hardcoded developer path. Makefile:764-769 shows the target's else-branch echoes 'not installed; skipping' and exits 0. Verified directly. This is the VACUOUS-PASS half: green in the Actions log while checking nothing.

Everything else inspects the checked-out tree, the installed venv, or shipped registries - none of which differ between laptop and runner. That includes agent-commit-range-check, which reads the commits a branch actually carries rather than resolved config.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND, deliberately not fixed here: uv-lock-revision-check compares HEAD:uv.lock against the working tree with no BASE_REF passed, so it is a no-op on ANY clean checkout - true for every develop-post-merge run. Not classified as an environment boundary issue because it is equally a no-op locally on a clean tree; fixing it means passing a real baseline ref (e.g. github.event.before) from develop-post-merge.yml, which is a separable change.

Decisions.

agent-identity -> SKIP on CI. Not 'adapt': there is no real developer identity on an ephemeral runner, so no synthetic input can make it meaningful - supplying one only swaps one always-passing input for another. Not 'keep failing': it was never meant to fail there.

skill-sync-check -> SKIP on CI. Its real CI coverage already exists and is untouched: pr.yml's guard-skill-sync-verify, a pinned-SHA network checkout running against every PR before it can reach develop.

agent-commit-range-check -> NEVER gated, per the item's must-preserve. Asserted in three separate tests plus the system parity test.

All other ~22 guards -> unchanged and unconditional.

MECHANISM: one declarative table (RUNNER_INAPPLICABLE_GUARDS) consulted uniformly, replacing the inline 'if [ $GITHUB_ACTIONS = true ]' one-off. It beats the inline pattern because the exception list becomes enumerable and testable in one place - the tests assert the table contains exactly the two documented slugs and that the recipe calls the gate exactly twice, so widening it is visible rather than diffuse. Adding a third exception is a table entry, not another copy-pasted conditional.

Implemented in 681a545020 (Sonnet subagent) + 6bab7554e9 (my review fixes). PR #1572.

REVIEW FOUND A BLOCKING DEFECT in the first implementation: the gate reproduced, one layer up, the exact defect it was written to remove. The recipe used the gate PROCESS as the 'if' condition - exit 0 run, exit 1 skip - so every way of failing to REACH a decision (uv absent, broken venv, script renamed, any traceback) also exits non-zero and was indistinguishable from a deliberate skip. The guard was then silently dropped with nothing recorded in 'failed'. Demonstrated rather than argued: 'if uv run -- python .../ci_lint_environment_gate_TYPO.py agent-identity' -> guard SILENTLY SKIPPED; 'PATH=/usr/bin:/bin uv run ...' -> guard SILENTLY SKIPPED. Fixed: decision travels on stdout as one token, recipe skips only on exact 'SKIP', anything else runs the guard, reason moved to stderr so it still reaches the Actions log.

SECOND REVIEW FINDING: gating agent-identity-check made the synthetic GIT_CONFIG identity dead, and tests/system/test_ci_lint_parity.py pinned that exact text including 'recipe.count(...) == 2'. Left alone it became a vacuous test asserting a behaviour that no longer happens, AND it blocked deleting the dead block. Shipping a newly vacuous test inside the change whose purpose is removing vacuous passes is self-defeating, so the item scope was widened to tests/system/** (reason recorded via scope-update) and the test now pins the gating and asserts the synthetic identity has NOT returned.

THIRD REVIEW FINDING: test_ci_lint_environment_boundary_cli_ignores_non_true_values asserted 'main() == 0' to mean 'run'. Under the new contract main always returns 0, so it had become vacuous. It now asserts the emitted decision token.

FALSIFICATION, three disjoint neuters:
1. Revert Makefile wiring, keep the module importable -> 3 wiring tests fail with AssertionError, not ImportError.
2. Keep wiring, make runs_on_runner always return True -> 3 classification/CLI tests fail.
3. Revert to the exit-status construct -> TestGateFailsClosed fails. This one is behavioural: it lifts the recipe's OWN lines, replaces the gate with an uninvokable command, and runs them in sh; the shell reports 'SKIPPED' where 'RAN' is required. An earlier version of this test failed with 'could not locate the gate condition' (a regex miss), which would not have survived a plausible rewrite - strengthened deliberately.

COVERAGE: two guards now run in zero places on CI, both previously vacuous there. Neither loses real coverage - agent-identity has no meaningful CI form anywhere, and skill-sync-check's real gate is pr.yml's guard-skill-sync-verify, unchanged. Every other guard including agent-commit-range-check is untouched and unconditional.

detail.evidence:
CORRECTION to this item's filed premise, established before any implementation began. I filed it claiming the sparse workflow set on published-results was why #1542 has zero checks. That is wrong. validate-submission.yml DOES live on published-results, DOES trigger on pull_request into it, and its 'paths: results-data/bundles/**' filter matches all 100 of #1542's changed files. It should have run.

REAL CAUSE: #1542's author is app/github-actions. sync-results-data-to-published.yml:195 opens it with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub never starts pull_request-triggered workflow runs for GITHUB_TOKEN events - documented recursion prevention, unreachable by any trigger filter. validate-submission.yml's own comment near line 56 already records that this mirror PR is opened with GITHUB_TOKEN; nobody had joined that to 'so this workflow never runs on it'.

The sparse-workflow cause is still real but is a SEPARATE, narrower gap: pr-base-guard.yml cannot fire on a published-results-based PR because its file is not there.

W0 CLASSIFICATION - what is meaningful for a corpus-only branch. published-results carries results-data/, benchbox/validation/bundle.py, scripts/validate_submission.py, scripts/generate_corpus_inventory.py and docs; nothing else. adr-published-results-slim-corpus-branch.md already rejected routing corpus contributions through develop's CI for this reason.
- MEANINGFUL: bundle schema/hash/privacy validation, and corpus-inventory freshness - exactly the two gates validate-submission.yml runs for a human submission PR.
- STRUCTURALLY INAPPLICABLE: ruff/ty/pytest matrix, packaging, browser and E2E lanes, docs build - none of the code they check exists on that branch.

Also confirmed by direct query, and it bounds what the fix can claim: no ruleset targets published-results. The repo's four rulesets target develop, release, v* branches and tags. So no check on that branch can be REQUIRED today; the draft state plus maintainer review is the actual enforcement.

Implemented in afb08886f2 (Sonnet subagent) + 4e5cab89eb (my review fixes). PR #1573.

FIX: the sync workflow validates the exact content it is about to propose - validate_submission.py plus generate_corpus_inventory.py --check, the same two gates validate-submission.yml would apply - and posts the verdict as a 'corpus-mirror/validate-bundles' commit status on the mirror branch head. A commit status is a Statuses-API write, not a workflow trigger, so it is unaffected by the GITHUB_TOKEN recursion rule and needs NO new credential; only a 'statuses: write' grant on the token the workflow already holds. A PAT or GitHub App was considered and rejected as introducing a credential the repo does not have.

SEQUENCING SOLVED: the fix lives entirely on develop. Storing published-results' workflow set on develop and having the sync workflow carry it over is not merely undesirable, it is not executable - GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push changes under .github/workflows/ regardless of the permissions block, which adr-published-results-slim-corpus-branch.md already documents for validate-submission.yml edits. So no develop-side test can assert published-results' content without going red until a human acts.

REVIEW FINDING - AVAILABILITY REGRESSION, fixed. The status and PR-opening steps sit after the new setup and validate steps, and GitHub skips every later step once one fails. A flaky setup-uv, or any error the validate step's 'set -uo pipefail' capture does not convert into a reported state, would have skipped BOTH: no status AND no mirror PR. That is strictly worse than the blind PR being fixed, because before these steps existed the PR was always created, and develop's Corpus Drift Check depends on that PR existing to be actionable. Both steps now run under always(); an absent verdict posts as 'error' rather than defaulting; the failure gate is '!= success' rather than '== failure' so a run that could not determine the verdict is not green. An absent verdict must never default to success - a green check on content nothing examined is worse than an empty rollup because it stops anyone looking.

NOT FIXED, documented as manual maintainer debt in docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md rather than left silent: pr-base-guard.yml still cannot run on a published-results-based PR.

LIMITS RECORDED so a green badge is not over-read: the status is ADVISORY (no ruleset targets published-results), and it is SELF-ATTESTED by the run that built the content, so it catches bad content but not a later manual push to the mirror branch. A --force-with-lease push from another run re-posts against the new SHA, so a stale green cannot ride on new bytes.

FALSIFICATION, two disjoint neuters: (1) rubber-stamping the validate step to STATE=success without invoking either validator, name/id/outputs unchanged - fails test_..._status_reflects_real_validation with 'validate step never invokes scripts/validate_submission.py'; (2) reverting the always() guards, the error default and the failure gate - fails exactly the 3 new availability tests while the other 6 pass.

SUITES: tests/unit/workflows 153 passed; test_stacked_pr_base_guard.py 5 passed; pr-base-guard.yml untouched and still unfiltered. check-scope OK, 3 files.

UNVERIFIED FROM HERE: no live GitHub run exercised the Statuses API call, so that the posted status renders in statusCheckRollup is asserted from documented API semantics and static structure, not integration-tested. The first mirror run after this lands is the confirming observation.

description.from:
Supersedes todo-wrapper-silently-falls-back-to-local-database, dropped the same day: verification ladders are
create-time-only in this tracker, so a lint finding on a rung can only be
fixed by recreating the item.

Running `_project/scripts/todo` with no TODO_DB_URL selects a local fallback at
.todo-db/todo.sqlite. `doctor` warns, but every other subcommand proceeds. That
local database sits at schema v3 while the CLI expects v5, so commands fail with
'database schema_version=3, CLI expects 5; run `todo migrate`'.

The failure mode is the dangerous part: the message points at a migration, which
invites an operator to run `todo migrate` -- or worse `todo init` -- against a
database that is NOT the tracker. On 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-31 this presented as
'the tracker is down' and two findings were written to out-of-tree drafts
instead of being filed. The hosted tracker was healthy the whole time (v5, 2045
items).

Contributing cause: .gitignore line 196 has a bare `.todo-db/` rule, which is
exactly what the todo-db bootstrap guide warns against because it hides the
committed .todo-db/config.json that would otherwise bind the hosted backend. No
config.json exists in this repo, so every session must supply TODO_DB_URL by hand.
description.to:
todo wrapper silently falls back to a stale local database when no backend is selected.

Coordination note (2026-08-05, after #1580 provision-local-tracker-db-auth):
Auto-provision now mints a hosted connection when turso is logged in and no backend is selected. That reduces how often the silent local path is hit for maintainers, but does NOT close this item: (1) auto-provision only helps when turso is present and mint succeeds; (2) the committed URL-only .todo-db/config.json + narrowed gitignore are still missing; (3) mutating commands should hard-error when no backend was selected, not warn-and-write. Implement against the new precedence: --db > TODO_DB_PATH > TODO_DB_URL > turso auto-provision > local fallback. Coordinate any todo_db.py changes with todo-db-auto-provision-mint-failure-visibility if touching the same resolve path.

make worktree-release FORCE=1 skips its own dirty check but still aborts on a dirty tree

description.from:
worktree-release-locked gates two refusals behind FORCE=1: the dirty-worktree check and the PR-not-MERGED check. But the release body then runs 'git checkout --detach origin/develop' as its first step, which git itself refuses when tracked files are modified:

  error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
      _project/scripts/green_unmerged_sweep.py
  Aborting
  make[1]: *** [worktree-release-locked] Error 1

So FORCE=1 advertises 'release this dirty worktree anyway' and cannot deliver it. Hit for real releasing pool-01 (branch fix/green-unmerged-all-required-checks, superseded WIP after #1633 merged); the workaround was to discard the changes by hand first, at which point FORCE=1 was only still needed for the no-PR check.

Fix options: (a) have the FORCE=1 path 'git reset --hard' (and optionally 'git clean -fd' for untracked) BEFORE the checkout, since FORCE=1 already means the operator accepts losing the work; or (b) drop the dirty bypass from FORCE=1 and make the refusal unconditional, so the flag stops promising something it cannot do. Note the reset already present later in the body runs too late to help.

Also worth deciding: 'git reset --hard' does not remove untracked files, so a released slot can still carry untracked leftovers (pool-01 had an obsolete _project/handoffs/*.md that survived until removed by hand).
description.to:
FORCE=1 on the pool targets advertises 'discard whatever is in the way and release/reset this slot'. It cannot deliver that today, in two distinct ways.

ROOT CAUSE (shared by both targets)
'git checkout --detach <ref>' refuses when a tracked file is modified and differs between HEAD and the target ref -- exactly the state FORCE=1 exists to bulldoze. Both recipes run the detach BEFORE any discard, so the recipe dies at its first step:

  error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
      _project/scripts/green_unmerged_sweep.py
  Aborting
  make[1]: *** [worktree-release-locked] Error 1

Hit for real releasing pool-01 (branch fix/green-unmerged-all-required-checks, WIP superseded once #1633 merged). Workaround was to 'git checkout -- <file>' by hand first; after that FORCE=1 was still needed, but only for the no-PR check.

MISSING FORCE ACTIONS, per target

worktree-release-locked (Makefile ~2016-2040) -- FORCE=1 gates only the two refusals; the body has NO discard actions at all:
  1. discard tracked modifications ('git reset --hard origin/develop') BEFORE the detach, not after it as now;
  2. remove untracked leftovers ('git clean -fdx -e .benchbox'). Absent entirely, so a released slot keeps them: pool-01 retained an obsolete _project/handoffs/*.md through the release and had to be cleaned by hand. Note the existing dirty CHECK already excludes .benchbox, so the clean must use the same exclusion or the two disagree.
  ('git branch -D' is already present and unconditional -- no change needed.)

worktree-pool-reset-locked (Makefile ~2216-2239) -- already HAS both force actions (clean -fdx -e .benchbox, and branch -D guarded against develop/main/release), so it is the reference for WHAT to do. But it shares the ordering defect: checkout --detach runs before reset --hard, so its FORCE=1 aborts on the same input. Prior-art decision: reuse its action set in worktree-release; fix the ordering in both.

FIX
Either discard first ('reset --hard' + 'clean' before the detach) or make the detach itself forceful ('git checkout --force --detach'). Prefer the former: it keeps the destructive step explicit and adjacent to the FORCE=1 guard, rather than hiding it in a flag on a checkout.

Do NOT relax anything outside the force path: the pool-NN-only guard and the develop/main/release refusal must stay unconditional, and without FORCE=1 a dirty or not-merged slot must still be refused. worktree-pool-reset's interactive 'Type RESET' confirmation is a deliberate extra brake on the more destructive target and should stay; worktree-release does not need one added.

Promoted from deferral #82 of provable-cli-command-generation.

description.to: Expanded from the original resolved-config CLI-command deferral after the 2026-08-08 architecture review reproduced a systemic quick-restart replay defect. Quick restart restores raw selectors after derived state has already been resolved and refreshes only tuning_resolution; platform_key, phases, tuning flags and files, unified config, organization payload, dataframe tuning, resolved mode, seed, BenchmarkConfig, preview metadata, and execution context can therefore disagree. First characterize the full replay contract, then introduce typed RunRequest and immutable ResolvedRunPlan models with one resolver, migrate quick restart as the first vertical slice, and finally migrate interactive, direct CLI, dry-run, load-only, preview, and canonical-record paths. Decision cases: explicit current CLI input overrides saved preferences; saved configuration is resolved atomically; missing historical optional fields use documented compatibility defaults; missing or invalid current configuration fails closed and executes nothing; a missing saved seed must be surfaced as non-exact replay; environment discovery is captured once or explicitly revalidated. Guard rails: no per-field synchronization patch, no second mutable SimpleNamespace representation, no CLI flag rename, no preview/execution divergence, no removal of compatibility attributes until static and behavioral evidence shows no consumer, no broad run.py cleanup, preserve explicit dry-run phases and deterministic seeds, and measure setup/dispatch overhead before and after.

After PR #759 moved `benchmark-runs-output-root-propagation` and
`benchmark-runs-local-artifact-guardrails` to DONE, the item
`benchmark-runs-duplicate-artifact-cleanup` (Medium-High) still has
`status: Not Started` with `deps.needs` pointing to both of those now-done
items. It is fully unblocked but nothing flagged it as ready to work.

This is a systemic gap: the TODO system has no automated step that detects
when a `deps.needs` item transitions to DONE and re-evaluates the downstream
item's readiness. The result is hidden unblocked work sitting in the backlog
looking like it's blocked.

Two deliverables:
1. An immediate fix — manually update `benchmark-runs-duplicate-artifact-cleanup`
   to reflect its newly-unblocked state.
2. A process fix — `todo_cli.py` already has a `ready` command (line ~486).
   Document its use in `_project/TODO/README.md` as a post-merge checklist
   step so the command is discoverable and unblocking transitions are caught
   automatically going forward.

description.to:
Managed UAT now uses an engine-resolved compose CLI: BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI overrides the choice, and on macOS mocker is selected when present before docker. Native Apple container tooling is used for container-store cleanup. This TODO is therefore not a migration task; it closes the remaining gap between the engine-agnostic implementation and release-grade managed-stack evidence.

The historical 2026-05-28 evidence remains unusable: the managed non-OLTP cells.jsonl was empty after a LakeSail startup timeout, and the managed OLTP run root was empty. Revalidate under the resolved managed engine, using Mocker on the current macOS path, into a fresh run root. Measure a healthy LakeSail compose-up before changing cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s, preserve the failure-capture-and-advance behavior, and run the managed tiers only in the release-gate order after native and dataframe stages. Each stack remains serialized and must produce up, run, and down lifecycle records plus non-empty result artifacts.

Mocker coverage is partial: QuestDB and PostgreSQL lifecycle parity plus QuestDB end-to-end execution are validated; Databend’s separate MinIO dependency has a known Mocker failure, while Doris and StarRocks still need separate Mocker validation. Use BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI=docker only for a stack with a documented Mocker incompatibility, and record the exception and evidence. Do not treat unit tests as full Mocker coverage.

Unblock by confirming Apple container and Mocker storage and memory headroom, measuring healthy LakeSail startup, setting cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s above that measurement with evidence, then running the managed smoke and release-gate rerun into a fresh root.

description.from: The tracker advertises a verification ladder per item and gates completion ('complete: complete an item (gated)'), but the gate does not execute the rungs. Two one-engine items are state=done at develop 9d1f899381 with rungs that fail when run by hand. one-engine-mcp-run-service-adoption: rung 1 ('! grep -n _map_phases_to_test_execution_type|_prepare_adapter_platform_options|_validate_and_resolve_mode benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py') fails because all three are still present at :98, :133, :171; rung 2 ('pytest tests/unit -k runplan and (equivalence or parity)') exits 5 because no test in the repository contains the string 'runplan'. one-engine-core-run-service: rung 4 ('! grep -rn l_shipdate|ss_sold_date_sk benchbox/cli/') fails on benchbox/cli/commands/convert.py:166 and :170. This is the systemic cause behind both defects being recorded as delivered work -- the ladder is authored carefully, then never run at the moment it would matter. Note the tracker already has a 'verify' verb that can run rungs, so the capability exists; it simply is not wired into the completion gate. Related: falsifiability lint was demoted to advisory in #1582, which removed the other automated check on rung quality.
description.to: BenchBox's active wrapper delegates lifecycle commands to the released todo-db package, whose complete command checks work units, deferrals, and blocks but does not execute the item's verification ladder. That lets completion accept failing or vacuous commands, including pytest exit 5 from an empty selector. Implement the gate in the canonical todo-db package so every consumer gets the same behavior: run the current ladder in order before completion, fail closed on any non-zero or indeterminate result, preserve the hosted-command trust boundary, and provide an explicit reason-bearing override recorded in the completion audit event. Existing done items stay terminal and are not retroactively reopened.

description.from: benchbox/core/run_service.py exports RunRequest, RunPlan and SilentVerbosity, all added in w2 (#1561). At develop 9d1f899381 their only importer anywhere is tests/unit/core/test_run_service.py. The live CLI path (BenchmarkOrchestrator.execute_benchmark -> execute_run) passes a BenchmarkConfig directly and never constructs a RunRequest or a RunPlan. They were forward scaffolding for MCP adoption, which one-engine-mcp-adoption-not-actually-done shows never happened, so they are now unreferenced types carrying an unreferenced test class. The tests in TestRequestAndPlanTypes assert frozen-dataclass behavior rather than BenchBox behavior: test_run_request_is_immutable asserts frozen=True, test_two_requests_with_the_same_inputs_are_equal asserts the generated __eq__, and test_run_plan_binds_a_request_to_its_resolved_config asserts that attributes just passed to a constructor can be read back. None can fail unless someone edits the dataclass decorators, so they consume fast-lane budget -- which cost a +500 ceiling bump in #1611 -- without buying regression protection. SilentVerbosity is the most defensible of the three since it was designed as the value MCP would pass.

description.from:
Deferred queue gate and spec handoff. This TODO does NOT implement a
queue directly. If Step 5 measurement returns BUILD QUEUE, this item
chooses the viable path and creates exactly one follow-up implementation
TODO from the locked spec below:

  - Path A: native GitHub Merge Queue
  - Path B: BenchBox Merge Steward

This shape is intentional. The TODO work-unit graph only supports
`pending`, `in_progress`, and `done`, so mutually exclusive Path A/Path B
implementation units cannot live in the same flat DAG without deadlocking
downstream work. The generated follow-up TODO becomes the executable
implementation item; this gate records the path and prevents re-debating
settled design decisions.

Status starts as Blocked (on Step 5). Three resolution paths:
  - Step 5 -> DO NOT BUILD: this TODO moves to DONE with completion note
    "queue not needed; closed by Step 5 measurement <date>"
  - Step 5 -> BUILD QUEUE: this TODO unblocks, status -> Not Started,
    work units below create the selected implementation TODO
  - Step 5 -> REASSESS: stays Blocked, deps point to next measurement

--- REFRESH 2026-07-23 (dev-loop-step-6-gate-refresh) ---
Re-homed from the retired YAML tracker (_project/TODO/**, removed in the hosted-DB migration) with design content preserved verbatim.
